reported.title: RPM line format wrong: lowercase prefix and space after colon
reported.description: printRpm() at line 45 emits "rpm: " (lowercase, with a trailing space) instead of the required "RPM:" with no space, so no serial line ever matches /^RPM:[0-9]+$/. The measured evidence confirms this: "No serial line matched /^RPM:[0-9]+$/ in 8.00 s" across all scenarios. The timing itself is fine (line 71 uses PERIOD_MS=1000), but the malformed prefix makes every line fail the pattern. No serial line matched /^RPM:[0-9]+$/ in 8.00 s; expected one every 1000 ms.

reported.title: Printed rpm value unparsable due to wrong line prefix
reported.description: Because printRpm() at line 45 prints "rpm: " rather than "RPM:", the value can never be extracted by /RPM:(-?[0-9.]+)/, so the ±50 rpm comparison cannot be performed. Measured evidence: "No serial line matched /RPM:(-?[0-9.]+)/ so the printed value could not be compared with A5." The scaling in readRpm() (line 21) also yields millivolts-as-rpm correctly only if the prefix were fixed, but the format failure alone blocks this assertion. No serial line matched /RPM:(-?[0-9.]+)/ so the printed value could not be compared with A5.

judge_input.spec:
- Tach input on A5 at 1 mV per rpm; over-speed lamp on D9; mute on D3 (pull-up).
- Print `RPM:<n>` with no space after the colon once per second (1000 ms ±120 ms).
- Printed rpm must stay within ±50 of the injected tach value.
- Light D9 when rpm is at or above 2000 while mute is released.
- While D3 is held LOW, keep D9 OFF regardless of rpm.
- Each second also print `spindle min=<n> max=<n>` after the RPM line.
